about: Company foundations, entered by hand. Each entry names a foundation by EIN (it must be in the IRS data), the company behind it, and, where the company's own giving page says so, the program a small nonprofit can apply to. serves lists the states a national program is open in ("*" for every state), so the foundation is shown there even when its IRS return lists other states. grantmatch/corporate.py checks this file. Change an entry only from the official page, and update its checked date.

program.name: Spark Good local grants
program.who: 501(c)(3) public charities, government entities, schools and faith-based groups with community-benefit projects, serving the same area as the Walmart store, Sam's Club or distribution center they ask. Needs a Spark Good account on Walmart.com, verified by Deed. 501(c)(4), (c)(6) and (c)(19) groups can't apply.
program.when: Three cycles a year: February 1 to April 15, May 1 to July 15, and August 1 to December 31 (one line on the page says November 30; confirm there). One grant per store or club per year.
program.how: Apply through your Spark Good account at walmart.com/nonprofits, choosing the nearby store, club or distribution center.
program.focus: Local needs, such as hunger relief, economic opportunity, sustainability, disaster response and community connection

program.name: Publix Super Markets Charities requests
program.who: Nonprofits that operate or serve clients in Florida, Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia or Kentucky. A staff or board member registers the organization.
program.when: Hunger relief requests March 1 to April 30 (decisions in September); housing and shelter requests July 1 to August 31 (decisions at year end); other requests any time.
program.how: Register once, and update yearly, on the Publix Charitable Donations site (charitabledonations.publix.com).
program.focus: Youth, education, hunger, homelessness and stronger communities

program.name: Truist Foundation grants
program.who: 501(c)(3) public charities in the United States, or applicants through a fiscal sponsor. Not for annual, scholarship or general operating requests. Three years between grants.
program.amount: At least $15,000 for local and regional grants
program.when: Deadlines March 31, July 31 and November 30 each year, with decisions about four months later.
program.how: Online portal from the foundation's grant application page, after an eligibility quiz.
program.focus: Career pathways for adults into middle-skill jobs, and support for small businesses

program.name: TD Charitable Foundation regional grants
program.who: Nonprofits in TD Bank's communities; Florida has its own giving contact. The eligibility rules are in the regional grants FAQ.
program.when: 2027 deadlines: March 12, May 14 and July 30, with decisions about two months later.
program.how: Online application through CyberGrants, from TD's funding opportunities page.
program.focus: Quality of life in TD's communities, including affordable housing and nonprofit capacity building

program.name: Albertsons Companies Foundation grants
program.who: Nonprofits in communities where Albertsons Companies stores operate (Albertsons, Safeway, Vons, Jewel-Osco and others). The online system sends each request to the regional team. Naming a store employee as a sponsor strengthens a request.
program.when: Requests outside a request for proposals can go in any time, for limited funds. Nourishing Neighbors requests for proposals use an invitation code. Answers come about six weeks after a cycle closes.
program.how: Online application from the foundation's community page. Check the Nourishing Neighbors page first for a current request for proposals.
program.focus: Hunger relief through Nourishing Neighbors, plus local community needs

program.name: Kroger Co. Foundation grants
program.who: 501(c)(3) nonprofits in communities Kroger and its stores serve. Request from one store brand only. Funding isn't guaranteed, and Kroger may give a different amount than asked.
program.when: Foundation grants are reviewed quarterly; the portal shows the next deadline. Allow about 12 weeks.
program.how: Create an account at communitygifts.com and choose Foundation Grant as the request type.
program.focus: Zero Hunger | Zero Waste, health and nutrition, and stronger communities

program.name: Duke Energy Foundation grants
program.who: Nonprofits serving communities where Duke Energy customers live and work, in the states Duke Energy serves. In Florida that means these counties: Alachua, Bay, Citrus, Columbia, Dixie, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Hardee, Hernando, Highlands, Jefferson, Lafayette, Lake, Leon, Levy, Liberty, Madison, Marion, Orange, Osceola, Pasco, Pinellas, Polk, Seminole, Sumter, Suwannee, Taylor, Volusia and Wakulla. Check the foundation's qualifications and restrictions first.
program.amount: Up to $20,000 for rolling grants; larger themed calls are announced from time to time.
program.when: Requests of $20,000 or less are taken year-round. Review can take three months or more.
program.how: Contact the foundation's grant representative for your state with your proposal before applying (in Florida, Loretta Murray; the contact link is on the foundation's Florida page). Then register and apply in the foundation's online grant system.
program.focus: Vibrant economies (energy workforce training, community revitalization, economic recovery), local resiliency (disaster preparedness and response, extreme weather resiliency, conservation and clean water), and community opportunity (upward economic mobility and access to opportunity for families in financial need)

program.name: Mosaic community investment grants
program.who: 501(c)(3) organizations near Mosaic's phosphate and potash operations and offices (in Florida, its Tampa headquarters and Central Florida mining and processing communities), with written nondiscrimination policies. Not for individuals, grantmakers, political, advocacy or private membership groups, endowment campaigns, or faith-based groups except community-wide charitable work. Mosaic prefers requests under 10% of the organization's budget and under 50% of the program's.
program.when: Four deadlines a year at midnight Eastern: March 20, June 22, September 21 and December 21, 2026, each with about four months of review (the December 21 round is decided by April 19, 2027).
program.how: Apply through Mosaic's online grant application for U.S. and Canadian organizations, linked from its community investment guidelines; one application covers The Mosaic Company and its foundation.
program.focus: Hunger and local food systems, agricultural education, habitat conservation, nutrient stewardship and watershed restoration, and the communities where Mosaic employees live and volunteer

program.name: Target Community Engagement Funds
program.who: 501(c)(3) public charities, and K-12 public, charter and nonprofit private schools and colleges with an NCES number. Target's store and distribution center leaders choose local grants. Target says most of its other grants are by invitation only.
program.when: Two cycles a year. In 2026: April 6 to May 6 (decided in July) and August 3 to September 4 (decided in November). Both are closed; the next cycle opens in April 2027.
program.how: Read the program guidelines, then apply from the Community Engagement Funds page while a cycle is open. An organization can have up to 10 applications at a time and can't apply for the same program in both cycles.
program.focus: Thriving families (basic needs, youth development), vibrant neighborhoods (community and green spaces), creative and cultural programming, and workforce development

program.name: Bank of America Charitable Foundation local grants
program.who: 501(c)(3) public charities based in and serving one of the bank's local markets (whole states in some places, single metro areas in others; in Florida these include Tampa Bay, Sarasota/Manatee, Central Florida, Jacksonville, Miami and more). Not eligible: private foundations, groups using a fiscal sponsor, government agencies, individual K-12 schools and their PTAs or foundations, endowments, memorial campaigns, and political, labor, fraternal or civic clubs. Applicants must register in NPO Hub and accept ACH payments.
program.amount: Varies by market and organization size; a past grant amount is a good starting point. Multi-year grants are generally not made through this process.
program.when: Two cycles a year; applications are not accepted outside them. In 2026: basic needs and income creation, February 2 to March 2 (decided in June); stable housing and empowering communities, May 18 to June 29 (decided in September). Watch the page for 2027 dates.
program.how: Check eligibility on the foundation's page; the eligibility quiz leads to the online application (CyberGrants). Apply to the one cycle that best fits your work. Questions go to foundation@bofa.com.
program.focus: Basic needs, income creation (jobs and workforce), stable housing, and empowering communities. Arts and environmental groups can apply when their work ties to these.
